creatorAcceptance.description: Creator workbench checks require an authorized interactive build-2227 run. They are recorded separately from automatic TF-ACCEPT markers so synthetic or source-only tests cannot claim native game coverage.

cases.description: F5 opens Sandbox while the Sandbox gamemode owns routing and opens CreatorTools only during stable standalone gameplay. Hide releases player controls while preserving the creator session; F5 reopens the same session.
The catalog spawns curated build-2227 items, UGC props, and every RobotKit robot type; search, kind filters, duplicate, transform, remove, undo, and End Session cleanup remain usable.
A native robot's location, autonomous personality, and brain mode can be previewed and are restored exactly when the session ends, without retaining native runtime handles in a project.

A test mod's authenticated character and validated self-contained vehicle factories spawn and unload safely. When no native vehicle adapter exists, the native vehicle source is visibly empty or degraded instead of inventing support.

Global mutation requires one explicit acknowledgement and a validated isolation lease. Save and checkpoint state are byte-for-byte unchanged after End Session; unavailable or revoked isolation fails closed and restores temporary changes.
A local visual event project loads, resolves its content, runs deterministic bounded branches, and Stop restores graph-owned spawns and edits while leaving unrelated manual session spawns intact.

Scene replacement, a Worlds transition or session, remote multiplayer admission, and mod unload close the global workbench and restore owned content, temporary native edits, controls, conversations, audio, and mutation isolation.
Unloading a custom content source removes its catalog entries and every produced instance exactly once in LIFO order; the open workbench prunes stale roster entries without crashing.

Ten open, spawn, edit, hide, reopen, graph run/stop, and End Session cycles complete with no retained objects, leases, bindings, input actions, UI surfaces, interactions, conversations, audio, callbacks, or save-state changes.
The initial active scene and its first scene-delivery callback are observed on the main thread.
Frame, fixed, and late callbacks are each delivered without cross-subscriber failure propagation.
Named keyboard, mouse, and gamepad actions report pressed, held, released, axes, conflicts, rebinding, and UI-focus suppression.
Player/camera aim, health damage/heal, and nested control leases operate and restore controls.
Ray/shape queries, entity transforms and motion, held-item operations, and native interaction prompts/callbacks operate through safe handles.
A package bundle and prefab load asynchronously, spawn through an opaque handle, and are destroyed without leaks.
Non-positional and positional framework audio cues play and release through lifetime-owned handles.
Validated config migration, installation-local typed storage, localization, commands, and diagnostics survive a reload.
HUD, window, modal, toast, high contrast, UI scale, reduced motion, focus, and teardown use TopiaForgeUi.
Scene/world/gamemode registration, loading, pause actions, session lifecycle, and save-aware teardown complete cleanly.
Robot spawn/body/health/movement, targets, objectives, dialogue, brain query, voice input, and custom interaction run without consumer native APIs.

The declared multiplayer module resolves through the extension boundary, binds generated state/command/event codecs, and executes them canonically through a ready interactive client-plus-server standalone loopback session.

Declared required providers and the installed optional UGC provider resolve exactly once; an absent optional dependency does not block the consumer; singleton conflicts, multiple-provider ordering, deterministic selection, and early release are enforced.
Unavailable or drifted game bindings return stable results and reasons without crashing the mod or startup.

Automatable core and noninteractive module resource families, including Creator Content sessions, complete ten in-session acquisition/release/reacquisition cycles with callback-stop and inactive-handle assertions. Hardware-, dialogue-, robot-, pause-, and session-specific handles are exercised by their dedicated live cases; offline lifecycle tests cover load/unload/reload and partial-load failure.
